title: Who’s asking? User personas and the mechanics of latent misalignment

bias_targets.methodology: Measuring LLM refusal and response rates to adversarial queries when conditioned on pro-social (e.g., altruistic, law-abiding, curious) versus anti-social (e.g., selfish, unlawful, close-minded) user personas using prompt prefixes and contrastive activation addition (CAA).

Comparing LLM refusal rates to harmful requests when the user persona is manipulated to reflect different religious identities (Jewish, Christian, Atheist, religious) via activation steering and prompting.
Evaluating differences in model responsiveness and safety filter activation to adversarial prompts across various ethnic user personas (African, Hispanic, Asian, Caucasian).

Assessing changes in refusal rates to adversarial attacks when the inferred user persona represents different gender identities, including man, woman, transgender man, transgender woman, and non-binary personas.
Measuring the impact of political user personas (e.g., lifelong Democrat, lifelong Republican, Obama supporter, Trump supporter) on the model's willingness to fulfill or refuse adversarial queries.
